title: Observability-Driven Safety Net for Model/Config Flips
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: Provide a safety net that combines streaming eval probes, statistical gating, and automatic policy actions (pause/rollback/route-weight-adjust) for staged model/config changes (canary & A/B). This system should be low-latency, minimize false positive rollbacks, and be auditable in the Console and runbooks.

Background: We've had several narrow regressions slip through canaries when metric drift was subtle (small but consistent quality degradation on narrow customer cohorts). Current rollout tooling lacks a unified, signal-rich guard that ties task-specific evals, production signals (latency, errors), and human review into a deterministic policy.

Scope:
- Build a runtime-safe "probe runner" that samples live traffic for canary/A-B cohorts and evaluates requests against a battery of lightweight checks (task eval metrics, toxicity/factuality proxies, stderr-rate, p95 latency).
- Implement sequential statistical tests (Bayesian credible intervals + sequential hypothesis testing) to decide whether a quality delta is statistically credible given traffic and effect size.
- Define policy primitives: pause, reduce-weight, full-rollback, escalate-to-human, continue. Policies must be configurable per-release and visible in Console.
- Wire the guard to the rollout controller so automatic actions are executed with metadata (triggering metric, cohort, test confidence) and recorded in audit logs.
- Provide dashboards and an on-call playbook + a Confluence runbook for triage and postmortems.

Key decisions to make:
- Use Bayesian sequential test (preferred) vs fixed-window frequentist A/B tests (trade-off: faster detection vs interpretability). We recommend Bayesian credible intervals with configurable threshold to lower false positives on low-volume cohorts.
- Which evals run inline vs async: keep latency-sensitive traffic path minimal (use asynchronous sampling for deep evals like full QA/human-like classifiers).
- Rollback hysteresis: require either (a) CI-triggered metric + 2 sequential checks OR (b) single check with >99% posterior probability of degradation.

Non-goals: full manual labeling workflow, long-running offline eval pipelines (those are separate), replacing existing console metrics (we integrate with them).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Probe runner deployed to canary stage and collecting eval samples for at least 3 different model types (completion, chat, embedding).
2) Statistical gate evaluates stream and emits decisions (continue/pause/rollback) with confidence metadata.
3) Automatic rollback action invoked in staging when policy is triggered and logged in audit trail.
4) Console dashboard shows per-release cohort health, probe-sample histogram, and decision timeline.
5) Playbook and Confluence runbook linked from rollout UI.
tasks: Design probe schema and sample selection strategy (stratified by route and geography)
Implement lightweight probe runner in serving runtime (sampling hooks + async eval queue)
Add sequential Bayesian test library and integrate with probe outputs
Define and implement rollout policy primitives (pause/reduce/rollback/escalate)
Instrumentation: emit decision events to tracing and audit logs with context
Console: add a "safety-net" view showing probes, statistical summaries, and action history
Write Confluence runbook + on-call escalation steps
End-to-end test: simulate degradation via traffic rewriter and verify automatic rollback
